matched_conditions: Same four frozen GGUF shards and checkpoint revision.
Same exact512/2048/8192 token-ID fixtures. MRS transports decoded text and asserts tokenizer round-trip; llama sends IDs.
Same BF16 KV, context16384, c1, temperature0,128 output tokens, no prefix cache, no MTP.
Same prefill chunk/batch sizes within the512 and8192 comparisons.
Both perform one full unmeasured fixture sweep followed by1warmup+3measured requests per prompt length.
Single active model, stopped rust-analyzer, no concurrent compiler or profiling in final measured windows.
Both use the same client timing formula: prompt_tokens/time_to_first_nonempty_text and127/(last-first text chunk time).
interpretation: No identified configuration mismatch invalidates the512/8192 engine comparisons.
Prefill throughput is end-to-end TTFT-derived, including HTTP, server scheduling and first-token computation; it is not a pure kernel throughput metric.
Decode outputs differ between engines, so MoE expert routing differs; these are fixed-prompt/fixed-length serving comparisons, not teacher-forced identical-token decode measurements.
Different numerical activation implementations are intrinsic to the engines; exact checkpoint bytes do not establish numerical or quality equivalence.
MRS additionally loads the vision projector, while llama is text-only; no vision inference runs. This consumes extra MRS memory, not a MRS performance advantage.
Separate process runs are serial rather than interleaved randomized trials;3measured cases per length do not provide confidence intervals.
512 and8192 are tested configurations, not an exhaustive optimum; distinguish matched configuration from best observed results.
Native ISQ4 runs must be separately labeled; they do not use identical weight quantization to UD-Q4_K_XL.
counting_note: MRS reads isolated metrics only outside the timing interval when stream usage is absent; llama uses stream usage. Both validate the same input/output counts and128 nonempty chunks.
